resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ because the first tower (1871) and the present tower (1906-1908, lit about 1907-08) are both given as the station's start. Reports show the concrete tower nearly finished in 1906-07 and its lantern due early 1908.

notes_for_editor: Thin official record before 1900 (the corpus starts in 1900), so 1871-1899 details rest on Lighthouse Friends (which cites the Department's annual reports and Fischer and Bouchard's book) and Quebec's heritage inventory. Names vary: Philip/Philippe Savage; Jean Batiste/Joseph Baptiste Caron. The Department's 'Cap Madeleine' entries in 1905-07 are the Trois-Rivieres village ranges and were not used. Disagreements: tower date (1906-08); diaphone date (1908 per LF, installed per volume printed 1910); lens status (LF: active to about 2000 and replaced, lens remains; Quebec 2009-10 and routedesphares: lens still operating; CCG lists a private aid). Keeper dates come from Lighthouse Friends (Quebec gives order only, plus Sasseville to 1923); 1886 appointment confirmed by the 1915-16 list matched by position in the OCR table (Sasseville, June 9, 1886, $980). The 1904 volume's OCR gives 1880 for the same entry (OCR error; later volumes say 1886). Heritage designation years (1988 federal building recognition, 2016 heritage lighthouse) are in the record but not confirmed in pages I could read, so the story gives no dates. 'access' / 'climbable' and the owner (Association Touristique vs. municipality) rely on tourism listings and should be checked. Measurements: Quebec gives 16.8 m/3.4 m; LF 17 m/3.5 m. Fact-check 2026-10-27: removed the 1900 Lloyd's sentence (that 'Cape Magdalen' is on Amherst Island, Magdalen Islands: same-name error) and source 11; Routedesphares is now source 11. Quebec's inventory does not itself date the concrete tower (it says the wooden tower was demolished about 1907).
